items.pronunciation_notes: The dot nasalises the long final vowel, so the word ends in a hum with no n sounded: nahiiṁ.

learn.explanation_en: नहीं is the ordinary negative, and its position is fixed: immediately before the verb, which in Hindi means near the end of the sentence. यह घर बड़ा नहीं है — this house is not big. English puts 'not' after the auxiliary and Hindi puts it in front of the whole verb, so the two land in different places even in a sentence this short.

examples.note: नहीं sits directly before the verb.
The same position with a feminine subject.
नहीं comes between the complement and the verb.

common_error.why_en: नहीं goes immediately before the verb, not before the adjective.

practice.question: चाय गरम ___ है।
practice.explanation_en: नहीं is the ordinary negative for a statement, and it goes before the verb.

game.explanation_en: नहीं belongs immediately before the verb, at the end of the sentence.

items.pronunciation_notes: In speech the two run together and the है is often barely audible, which is part of why it can vanish altogether.
items.gloss_en: negating होना, and the dropped verb

learn.title_en: नहीं है — and when the है disappears
learn.explanation_en: When नहीं negates होना, the verb is very often dropped altogether. यह अच्छा नहीं है and यह अच्छा नहीं both mean 'this is not good', and the shorter one is extremely common in speech. Nothing is lost, because नहीं already stands where the verb would have been. This shortcut belongs to होना alone — it does not happen with other verbs.

examples.note: The full form, with the verb present.
The same meaning with है dropped.
In the plural the verb is usually kept.

common_error.why_en: नहीं comes before the verb, never after it. Dropping the verb is fine; moving it is not.

practice.question: यह अच्छा ___ है।
practice.explanation_en: A statement takes नहीं, placed just before the verb.

game.explanation_en: नहीं sits between the adjective and the verb. Nothing may follow the verb.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two unstressed syllables run together, with the nasal hum closing the phrase.

learn.explanation_en: नहीं on its own is a complete answer: 'no'. Adding जी makes it courteous — जी नहीं is the polite refusal, and जी हाँ is its opposite. Between friends a bare नहीं is perfectly fine; with a stranger or an elder, जी नहीं is safer, and it costs one extra syllable. This is the same जी you met attached to पिता and दादी.

examples.note: The courteous refusal.
Its opposite, built the same way.
नहीं twice — once as an answer, once inside the sentence.

common_error.why_en: जी comes first in this fixed pair, exactly as it does in जी हाँ.

practice.question: ___ नहीं।
practice.explanation_en: जी comes before नहीं and turns a blunt refusal into a courteous one.

game.question_en: Which is the polite way to say no?
game.explanation_en: जी नहीं is the fixed pair. The order matters, and न and मत do not fit here at all.

summary.recap_en: This level covered नहीं, the ordinary negative. It goes immediately before the verb, it can absorb होना entirely in speech, and जी नहीं is its polite form.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the two other negatives, and when each of the three is required.

items.pronunciation_notes: A single short syllable with a dental न — the tongue on the teeth, not curled back.
items.gloss_en: a softer negative, and a tag

learn.explanation_en: न is a shorter, softer negative than नहीं. Its most useful job for a learner is as a tag at the end of a sentence, asking the listener to agree: यह अच्छा है न? — 'this is good, isn't it?'. It also replaces नहीं in formal and poetic writing. As a plain negative in ordinary speech, stay with नहीं and keep न for tags.

examples.note: न as a tag, inviting agreement.
The same tag with a polite subject.

examples.english: The tea is hot, isn't it?
examples.note: A tag turns a statement into a check.

common_error.why_en: For ordinary negation use नहीं. न in that slot sounds formal or poetic rather than neutral.

practice.question: यह अच्छा है ___?
practice.explanation_en: न at the end of a statement turns it into a request for agreement.

game.question_en: Which sentence asks 'This is good, isn't it?'
game.explanation_en: As a tag, न comes after the complete sentence, not inside it.

items.pronunciation_notes: A dental त with the tongue on the teeth, and the final vowel drops: mat.

learn.explanation_en: मत is the negative used only with commands: मत जाओ, don't go. It cannot negate an ordinary statement — यह मत है is not Hindi at all. The command forms themselves arrive in Module 7, so for now treat मत as recognition rather than production: when you see or hear it, someone is being told not to do something. You will meet it on signs long before you need to say it.

examples.note: मत before the command form of जाना.
The same pattern with करना.
The place comes first, and मत sits just before the verb.

common_error.why_en: Commands take मत, not नहीं. The two are not interchangeable in either direction.

practice.question: ___ जाओ।
practice.explanation_en: Commands are negated with मत, which is what it exists for.

game.explanation_en: मत negates a command, नहीं negates a statement, and the two never stack together.

items.pronunciation_notes: All three are short and unstressed, and in fast speech नहीं can shorten until it sounds close to न.

learn.explanation_en: नहीं negates ordinary statements and is the one you will use most. न is softer: mainly a tag asking for agreement, and a formal alternative elsewhere. मत is only ever for commands. Their jobs do not overlap, so the choice is settled by what kind of sentence you are building rather than by how strongly you mean it — which makes this easier than it first looks.

examples.note: A statement, so नहीं.
A tag, so न.
A command, so मत.

common_error.why_en: मत only negates commands. A statement always takes नहीं.

practice.question: यह अच्छा ___ है।
practice.explanation_en: This is a statement rather than a command or a tag, so it takes नहीं.

game.question_en: Which sentence uses the right negative?
game.explanation_en: Only one option matches its negative to its sentence type: a statement with नहीं.

summary.recap_en: This level completed the negatives. नहीं for statements, न for tags and formal writing, मत for commands — three words whose jobs do not overlap, so the sentence type decides which you need.
summary.next_up_en: Next: word order, and why the verb never moves.

items.pronunciation_notes: Four short words with the verb last and unstressed, which is the rhythm of almost every Hindi sentence.

learn.explanation_en: Hindi is head-final: the verb comes last and everything else stacks up in front of it. A phrase saying where something is goes near the front, the subject follows, and the verb closes the sentence. घर में किताब है is literally 'house-in book is'. English fronts the verb and trails the location, so the two languages build the same thought in almost opposite orders, and the habit takes a while.

examples.english: There is a book in the house.
examples.note: Location, then subject, then verb.

examples.english: There is tea on the table.
examples.note: The same shape with a different postposition.

examples.english: There are children in the house.
examples.note: A plural subject takes a plural verb, and the order does not change.

common_error.why_en: The verb goes last in Hindi, so nothing may follow it.

practice.question: घर ___ किताब है।
practice.explanation_en: The book is inside the house, so the postposition is में.

game.explanation_en: The verb must come last, and में must follow the noun it belongs to.

items.pronunciation_notes: Five words in a single breath group, with the stress falling on नई rather than on the verb.

learn.explanation_en: Longer sentences are built by adding more in front of the verb, never after it. मेज़ पर नई किताब है has a location, an adjective, a noun and a verb, in that order. Each new piece slots in before whatever came after it, and the verb stays exactly where it was. If you can keep the verb last, the rest of the order will mostly take care of itself.

examples.english: There is a book on the table.
examples.note: The basic frame.

examples.english: There is a new book on the table.
examples.note: An adjective added in front of the noun.

examples.hindi: मेज़ पर दो नई किताबें हैं।
examples.read_as: mez par do naii kitaabeṁ haiṁ.
examples.english: There are two new books on the table.
examples.note: A number added, and the verb turns plural.

common_error.why_en: किताब is feminine, so नया has to take its irregular feminine form नई.

practice.question: मेज़ पर ___ किताब है।
practice.explanation_en: किताब is feminine, and this adjective's irregular feminine is नई.

options: नई किताब मेज़ पर है नहीं।
options_read_as: naii kitaab mez par hai nahiiṁ.
game.explanation_en: The adjective must agree with किताब, the postposition must follow मेज़, and nothing may come after the verb.

tts_strings: मेज़ पर दो नई किताबें हैं।

items.pronunciation_notes: The क्या at the front is unstressed, and the sentence rises at the end rather than in the middle.

learn.explanation_en: English rearranges a sentence to make a question — 'there is a book' becomes 'is there a book'. Hindi does not. क्या goes at the front and everything else stays exactly where it was, verb included. That is one of the genuinely easy things about Hindi: you add a word rather than rebuilding the sentence, and the word order you have just learned carries straight over.

examples.english: There is a book on the table.
examples.note: The statement.

examples.english: Is there a book on the table?
examples.note: क्या added at the front, and nothing else touched.
क्या in the middle asks 'what' instead.

common_error.why_en: The verb stays at the end in questions too. Only क्या is added, and only at the front.

practice.question: ___ मेज़ पर किताब है?
practice.explanation_en: क्या at the front turns the statement into a yes-or-no question without moving anything.

game.question_en: Which sentence asks 'Is there a book on the table?'
game.explanation_en: क्या goes at the front and the verb stays at the end. The third option asks what the book is instead.

summary.recap_en: This level set out Hindi word order. The verb comes last, everything else stacks up in front of it, and questions add a word rather than rearranging anything.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the connectors that join two sentences into one, which closes the module.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both sit between the clauses and take a small pause before them, which is how you hear where one sentence ends.

learn.explanation_en: और joins two things — you have used it since Module 4 for joining nouns, and it joins whole sentences in exactly the same way. लेकिन contrasts them: 'but'. Both sit between the two clauses, where English puts them too, which makes these two of the easiest words in the module. Note that पर can also mean 'but', so the postposition पर and the conjunction पर are told apart by position alone.

examples.hindi: चाय गरम है और मिठाई ताज़ी है।
examples.read_as: chaay garam hai aur miṭhaaii taazii hai.
examples.english: The tea is hot and the sweets are fresh.
examples.note: Two complete sentences joined by और.

examples.hindi: चाय गरम है लेकिन मिठाई ठंडी है।
examples.read_as: chaay garam hai lekin miṭhaaii ṭhaṇḍii hai.
examples.english: The tea is hot but the sweets are cold.
examples.note: लेकिन marks the contrast between them.

examples.hindi: घर बड़ा है लेकिन साफ़ नहीं है।
examples.read_as: ghar baṛaa hai lekin saaf nahiiṁ hai.
examples.english: The house is big but not clean.
examples.note: The second clause is negated.

common_error.wrong: चाय गरम है और ठंडी है।
common_error.right: चाय गरम है लेकिन ठंडी नहीं है।
common_error.why_en: और joins things that agree with each other. A contradiction needs लेकिन.

practice.question: चाय गरम है ___ मिठाई ठंडी है।
practice.question_read_as: chaay garam hai ___ miṭhaaii ṭhaṇḍii hai.
practice.explanation_en: The two halves contrast with each other, so the connector is लेकिन.

options: चाय गरम है और ठंडी है।
चाय गरम है लेकिन मिठाई ठंडी है।
options_read_as: chaay garam hai aur ṭhaṇḍii hai.
chaay garam hai lekin miṭhaaii ṭhaṇḍii hai.
game.explanation_en: लेकिन goes between two complete clauses, and the first option contradicts itself.

tts_strings: चाय गरम है और मिठाई ताज़ी है।
चाय गरम है लेकिन मिठाई ठंडी है।
घर बड़ा है लेकिन साफ़ नहीं है।

items.pronunciation_notes: क्योंकि opens with the same क्य stack as क्यों, and इसलिए runs to three quick syllables.

learn.explanation_en: क्योंकि means 'because' and introduces a reason. इसलिए means 'therefore' and introduces a result. They point in opposite directions, so which one you need depends on which clause you have put first. क्योंकि also finally lets you answer a क्यों question — you have been able to ask why since level fourteen, and this is the word that lets someone reply.

examples.hindi: चाय अच्छी है क्योंकि गरम है।
examples.read_as: chaay achchhii hai kyoṁki garam hai.
examples.english: The tea is good because it is hot.
examples.note: The reason comes after क्योंकि.

examples.hindi: चाय गरम है इसलिए अच्छी है।
examples.read_as: chaay garam hai isliye achchhii hai.
examples.english: The tea is hot, therefore it is good.
examples.note: The same two facts with the order reversed.

examples.hindi: यह घर बड़ा है इसलिए महँगा है।
examples.read_as: yah ghar baṛaa hai isliye mahãgaa hai.
examples.english: This house is big, so it is expensive.
examples.note: इसलिए introduces the consequence.

common_error.wrong: चाय गरम है क्योंकि अच्छी है।
common_error.right: चाय अच्छी है क्योंकि गरम है।
common_error.why_en: क्योंकि introduces the reason, so the reason has to be the clause that follows it.

practice.question: चाय अच्छी है ___ गरम है।
practice.explanation_en: The second clause gives the reason for the first, so the connector is क्योंकि.

game.question_en: Which sentence means 'The tea is good because it is hot'?
options: चाय अच्छी है क्योंकि गरम है।
चाय अच्छी है इसलिए गरम है।
चाय गरम है क्योंकि अच्छी है।
चाय गरम है इसलिए ठंडी है।
options_read_as: chaay achchhii hai kyoṁki garam hai.
chaay achchhii hai isliye garam hai.
chaay garam hai kyoṁki achchhii hai.
chaay garam hai isliye ṭhaṇḍii hai.
game.explanation_en: The reason must follow क्योंकि. Swapping the connector or the clauses reverses the logic.

tts_strings: चाय अच्छी है क्योंकि गरम है।
चाय गरम है इसलिए अच्छी है।
यह घर बड़ा है इसलिए महँगा है।

items.pronunciation_notes: फिर opens with an aspirated फ, and तो is so unstressed in speech that it often almost disappears.

learn.explanation_en: फिर means 'then' in the sense of next: one thing after another. तो is looser — it can mean 'so' or 'then', and in conversation it very often carries no meaning at all, working as a filler that softens whatever follows. Both are extremely common, and तो in particular is a word you will hear far more often than you can define. Do not worry about pinning it down; notice where it falls and copy that.

examples.note: फिर asking what comes next.
तो introducing a conclusion.

examples.hindi: चाय गरम है तो अच्छी है।
examples.read_as: chaay garam hai to achchhii hai.
examples.english: The tea is hot, so it is good.
examples.note: तो linking a condition to its result.

common_error.why_en: क्योंकि has to be followed by a reason and cannot be left at the end of a sentence.

practice.question: ___ क्या?
practice.explanation_en: फिर means 'then' in the sense of what happens next.

game.question_en: Which sentence means 'The tea is hot, so it is good'?
options: चाय गरम है लेकिन अच्छी है।
चाय गरम है और अच्छी है।
चाय गरम है तो अच्छी है।
चाय गरम है क्योंकि अच्छी है।
options_read_as: chaay garam hai lekin achchhii hai.
chaay garam hai aur achchhii hai.
chaay garam hai to achchhii hai.
chaay garam hai kyoṁki achchhii hai.
game.explanation_en: All four are grammatical, but only तो gives the sense of one thing following from another.

tts_strings: चाय गरम है तो अच्छी है।

summary.recap_en: This level closed Module 5 with the connectors. और joins, लेकिन contrasts, क्योंकि gives a reason, इसलिए gives a result, फिर marks sequence, and तो does a bit of everything — which is why it is the one you will hear most.
key_forms: चाय गरम है लेकिन ठंडी नहीं है।
चाय अच्छी है क्योंकि गरम है।
summary.next_up_en: Module 6 takes on the oblique case — the second form every Hindi noun has, and the reason this module could only use nouns that never change.
